USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Painful blurred vision after treatment begins

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 31-year-old man develops bilateral blurred vision and eye pain 12 days after starting topiramate. Examination shows an acute myopic shift, shallow anterior chambers, and elevated intraocular pressures. Which diagnosis best unifies the ocular findings and medication history?

  1. Primary open-angle glaucoma
  2. Migraine visual aura
  3. Drug-associated secondary angle-closure glaucoma
  4. Optic neuritis
  5. Retinal detachment
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Drug-associated secondary angle-closure glaucoma

Topiramate can cause an acute myopic shift with secondary angle closure, requiring urgent assessment.

Understanding the options

Drug-associated secondary angle-closure glaucoma
Topiramate can cause an acute myopic shift with secondary angle closure, requiring urgent assessment.
Optic neuritis
Optic nerve inflammation does not explain shallow chambers and high intraocular pressure.
Retinal detachment
A retinal lesion does not explain bilateral anterior chamber shallowing.
Primary open-angle glaucoma
This is usually gradual and does not cause this acute myopic syndrome.
Migraine visual aura
Aura does not account for persistent objective pressure elevation.
